results.title: Sora System Card
results.rule_cited: §1 carve-out — named external evaluator (ScaleAI, listed under 'Red Teaming Organizations') contributed findings; filed under that evaluator, Scope third-party-evaluator, Finding Type modifier company-published. OpenAI's own surrounding self-assessment remains a hard drop.
results.external_evaluator: ScaleAI — named in the Acknowledgements under 'Red Teaming Organizations:'. Twenty external red teamers are also named individually (Alexandra García Pérez, Arjun Singh Puri, Caroline Friedman Levy, Dani Madrid-Morales, Emily Lynell Edwards, Grant Brailsford, Herman Wasserman, Javier García Arredondo, Kate Turetsky, Kelly Bare, Matt Groh, Maximilian Müller, Naomi Hart, Nathan Heath, Patrick Caughey, Per Wikman Svahn, Rafael González-Vázquez, Sara Kingsley, Shelby Grossman, Vincent Nestler). ScaleAI is the only named organisation; no government AISI contributed, so Scope = third-party-evaluator. Caveat for the ledger: the External Red Teaming section attributes results to 'red teamers' collectively rather than to ScaleAI by name in-line, so the org-to-finding link runs through the acknowledgements list.

findings.finding: External red teamers found that framing prompts in medical or science-fiction/fantasy settings degraded Sora's safeguards against generating erotic and sexual content, and that adversarial prompting (suggestive phrasing, metaphor, iterating on words that trigger safeguards, then reusing the most-concerning generation as seed media) produced violative content unobtainable with single-prompt techniques, until further mitigations were built.
findings.finding_quote: For example, red teamers found that using text prompts with either medical situations or science fiction / fantasy settings degraded safeguards against generating erotic and sexual content until additional mitigations were built.
findings.tier_reasoning: Empirical model finding (observed behaviour under red-team testing); names a specific model and company (Sora, OpenAI); a demonstrated safeguard bypass producing prohibited sexual content is concerning and a company response is reasonable to expect — the card itself records mitigation work, which is a response, not a reason to downgrade (§8 negative-lag, pre-deployment). §4b not engaged: this is limb 1, a safeguard bypass, not an accuracy/hallucination finding. FRONTIER-MODEL RULE met — Sora is a named frontier multimodal generative model, not product ML. Derived: yes/yes -> A. [CLUBBED: the contextual-framing degradation and the adversarial-prompting/seed-media escalation are answered by the same mitigation package (prompt filtering, blocklists, classifier thresholds), §5 club test.]

findings.finding: External red-team testing of Sora's media-upload path and its storyboard, recut, remix and blend tools revealed gaps in input and output filtering, and showed that non-violative uploaded media could be modified into prohibited erotic, violent or deepfake content, requiring stronger classifier filtering before release.
findings.finding_quote: Red teamers also tested media uploads and Sora’s tools (storyboards, recut, remix, and blend) with both publicly available images and AI-generated media. This revealed gaps in input and output filtering to strengthen prior to Sora’s release, and helped hone protections for media uploads including people. Testing also revealed the need for stronger classifier filtering to mitigate the risk of non-violative media uploads being modified into prohibited erotic, violence, or deepfake content.
findings.tier_reasoning: Empirical model finding on a named model/company (Sora, OpenAI); distinct from the prompt-side bypass and warrants a distinct response (upload input/output filtering and classifier thresholds rather than prompt filtering), so split per §5. Concerning: non-violative uploads convertible into deepfake/erotic/violent output is a safeguard failure with real-world misuse potential — §4b limb 1 (safeguard bypass) and limb 3 (harmful manipulation in a societal setting); not an ordinary-accuracy finding. Frontier model rule met. Derived: yes/yes -> A.
